newsitem.title: UK: Sterling hovers at lows in Europe, eyes on EU summary.
newsitem.headline: Sterling hovers at lows in Europe, eyes on EU summary.

text.p: Sterling stumbled in Europe, sliding near one pfenning from its perch around 57-month highs of 2.8440 marks re-visited earlier.
Profit-taking and optimism over European Union nations reaching an agreement over the key stability pact at the EU summit in Amsterdam both weighed on sterling, said analysts.

"Comments suggest that a compromise has been reached between the German and French...It suggests EMU is on track and sterling may have lost a bit of ground," said Nick Stamenkovic economist at DKB International.
At 1005 GMT sterling stood at 2.8363/70 marks.
This compared with session and 57-month peaks of 2.8440 marks hit earlier and 2.8440/50 in late Europe on Friday.
Against the dollar, cable stood at $1.6352/62 against $1.6371/76 in late Europe on Friday.

A buoyant sterling, which marched on Friday to its highest against the mark since August 1992, has benefited from its status as a safe-haven currency in the face of uncertainty over European monetary union and from interest rate differentials.
"Sterling is taking a bit of a breather. But I think it will remain pretty well underpinned ahead of the (UK) budget," said DKB's Stamenkovic.
Markets are expecting a tough budget from the new Labour government on July 2 - and while tighter fiscal policy will help dampen inflation, higher interest rates are also expected.
"The market is still anticipating higher rates. The differentials between the UK and Europe should continue to widen," said a trader at a Belgian bank.

UK shares on Monday were hit by reports the government's first budget would target corporate sector. The FTSE 100 stock index, which notched up three all-time closing highs last week, was down 31.3 points to 4,751.8.
The Financial Times said on Monday the Treasury was considering abolishing a 20 percent tax credit on dividend payments.
"We saw sterling/mark above 2.84 this morning...We are back down on short-term profit-taking, but it is being well bid on the dips," said the trader.

A slightly easier dollar/mark, which edged lower to just above 1.73 on Monday, was also said to be dragging down sterling/mark. But analysts said if markets perceived the mark would eventually be swallowed up by a weak euro, then both sterling and the dollar were set to move higher.
